history.content: What are the challenges facing the installation of the HEL HA Add-On cluster?

The challenge facing the installation of the RHEL HA Add-On cluster in an IBM Cloud Classic Infrastructure environment is the unavailability of network-based access to remote management devices through the Intelligent Platform Management Interface (IPMI) due to enterprise security. As a result, shared storage devices are used for fencing of cluster nodes to ensure a quorum. These shared storage devices are implemented by deploying an iSCSI LUN to your servers as a quorum device. Additionally, IBM Cloud Block Storage has built-in HA capabilities, so a single shared iSCSI LUN does not introduce a Single Point Of Failure (SPOF) because your network layout is redundant. However, the specifics of your cluster product might require multiple quorum devices.

SAP HANA (High-performance ANalytic Appliance) is a multi-model database that stores data in memory rather than on disk. This design leads to data processing that is significantly faster than that of traditional disk-based data systems, enabling advanced real-time analytics. SAP HANA can be deployed on SAP NetWeaver within the IBM Cloud® environment. It is an in-memory database installed on a dedicated database server. The main architectural configurations for SAP HANA include single-host and multiple-host systems. Additionally, IBM Cloud is certified to run SAP NetWeaver application servers, including ABAP, Java, and various SAP products based on these application server stacks.

SAP NetWeaver serves as the core foundation of the SAP technology stack and is the platform utilized for Advanced Business Application Programming (ABAP) and Java applications. The components of SAP NetWeaver are built on the SAP NetWeaver Application Server and are developed using either ABAP or Java Platform, Enterprise Edition. It’s important to note that ABAP systems, Java systems, and dual-stack systems are distinct and separate entities.
